breakdown.description: The prompt replaces the unit force required for a deflection calculation with a unit moment; in the unit-load method, the virtual load must match the type and direction of the desired displacement.
breakdown.reason: The agent correctly identified that a unit load, not a unit moment, is required to calculate deflection using the virtual work method. The generated text specifies using a 'unit point load (1 N) downward at x = 2000 mm', which aligns with the ground truth's approach.

breakdown.description: The prompt treats simple supports as zero-rotation boundaries, even though a simply supported beam is free to rotate at its supports.
breakdown.reason: The agent failed to resolve this inconsistency and repeated the user's incorrect instruction. The generated specification states, 'Both the real and auxiliary systems have simple supports modeled as zero-rotation boundaries.' This is physically incorrect, as simple supports allow rotation.
